title: 融资高企，意味着股市即将下跌吗？
title_en: Does High Margin Debt Signal a Stock Market Decline?
author: Taiyang Feng (Sunny)
summary: 融资有周期，但没有固定的倒计时。在我们的美股检验中，保证金融资与价格信息高度重叠，尚未提供稳定的额外择时依据。
summary_en: Borrowing has cycles, but no fixed countdown. In our US tests, margin-financing measures overlap substantially with price information and have not provided a stable additional basis for market timing.
articleBody:
融资余额创新高，常常被解读为市场过热；融资开始回落，又容易让人联想到下一场大跌。这个故事很有吸引力：借钱买股票推高价格，随后去杠杆把涨幅还回去。

但对投资者来说，关键的问题是：**融资数据有没有告诉我们，价格还没有告诉我们的事？**

我们从美国保证金融资的长期变化入手，比较了不同融资状态之后的收益、最大回撤和波动。研究的落点很清楚：融资的起落容易看见，要把这些起落变成稳定的进出场依据，却困难得多。

## 有周期，不等于有倒计时

扣除通胀后，融资余额仍然反复扩张、收缩，再重新扩张。1997—2024 年，按统一的 10% 反转规则，我们在两个报告口径区间内识别出九段收缩及其后的恢复扩张。

这些过程长短不同。仅从峰值到谷底，收缩就有两个月结束的，也有持续三十个月的。融资周期描述了借贷行为的变化，却没有给下一次市场下跌安排日期。

![图 1｜融资反复扩张与收缩。两段分别以起点为 100，用于观察各自的变化，不比较两段之间的绝对水平。来源：FINRA、CPI，Residual Inertia 计算。](assets/insights/margin-debt-cycles-zh.svg)

融资高位同样需要说明“相对什么”。美元金额、相对市场规模的存量、融资增长速度，回答的是不同问题。我们用 ΔDC 观察扣除通胀后的融资增长，用 ΔDS 观察融资相对股价的增长，分别检验，而没有把两个指标当作两次独立确认。

其中，ΔDS 高位之后的回撤差异较醒目：未来十二个月的平均最大回撤约为 22.2%，全部可用起点的基准约为 16.0%，相差 6.2 个百分点。

可是，去掉与 2007—2009 年金融危机重叠的观察窗口后，高位组为 15.7%，基准为 14.1%，差距缩小到 1.5 个百分点。

![图 2｜ΔDS 高位后的回撤差异，很大一部分集中在金融危机。最大回撤是持有期内从高点到随后低点的最大损失，不是期末收益。来源：FINRA、CRSP，Residual Inertia 计算。](assets/insights/margin-debt-drawdowns-zh.svg)

危机本身当然重要。但如果一个指标的吸引力主要来自少数危机，它能否在下一轮、以同样的规则提前发挥作用，就仍是另一个问题。我们的检验尚未找到稳定的答案。

## 融资里，已经包含了多少价格信息？

融资与价格一起变化，并不意外。市场上涨会改变账户权益、借贷空间和投资者借钱的意愿；市场下跌时，这些条件又会反过来变化。对 ΔDS 来说，股价还直接进入了指标的计算。

在我们的样本中，2010 年以前，价格领先融资的跨月关系比较清楚；此后，同月联动更强。进一步把已知的价格趋势、近期收益和事前波动放进比较后，融资收缩原本看起来较高的后续风险，不再呈现清楚的独立差异。

**这意味着，同一轮价格变化，可能先出现在行情里，又出现在融资数据里。看到了两个指标，不一定就得到了两份新信息。**

也有值得保留的例外：在美国样本里，相近的价格状态下，融资仍增长但增速放缓的月份，表现好于融资继续加速的月份。这是一项有意思的条件差异，但还不是经过独立样本验证的交易规则。

对投资者来说，融资数据依然可以帮助理解市场参与者正在怎样调整借贷。只是，融资高位并不自动等于卖点，融资下降也不自动等于风险已经出清。保证金账户之外，期权等工具仍可能十分活跃；成交活跃本身又不等于净杠杆增加。

因此，在价格之外加入一个融资指标之前，最值得先问的是：**它提供了新的判断依据，还是换了一种方式，重复价格已经显示的变化？** 就我们检验过的保证金融资指标而言，前者目前仍然有限。

## 方法与数据

本文是既有研究的公众版解读，沿用冻结至 2024 年末的数据和检验，没有为本文重新挑选参数。保证金融资指客户证券保证金账户的借款余额，不包括全部衍生品敞口，也不同于上市公司的负债。

图 1 使用月度融资余额除以 CPI。1997 年 1 月至 2010 年 1 月采用历史合并数据，2010 年 2 月后采用 FINRA 统一报告数据；两段各自归一化。周期划分在各段内进行：较运行峰值下跌 10% 确认收缩，较随后运行谷底上涨 10% 确认恢复扩张。峰谷日期是回顾性描述，确认日期更晚。

D 为名义融资余额，P 为标普 500 价格指数，CPI 为消费价格指数。ΔDC = 100 × [(D/CPI)t ÷ (D/CPI)t−12 − 1]；ΔDS = 100 × [(D/P)t ÷ (D/P)t−12 − 1]。D/P 不是融资余额除以全市场市值。

图 2 的高位是 ΔDS 超过同一报告口径内、仅使用此前历史计算的 80 分位，至少需要 24 个有效历史观察。信号月份为 t，在 t+1 月末进入，观察至 t+13 月末；使用 CRSP 的 SPY 日度含分红收益计算财富路径及最大回撤。信号起点为 2000 年 1 月至 2010 年 1 月、2013 年 2 月至 2023 年 11 月。全样本 251 个起点，其中高位 39 个；剔除前瞻持有窗口与 2007 年 10 月至 2009 年 3 月相交的观察后，分别为 221 和 25 个。基准包含高位起点，不能读作高位组与正常组的对照。

图中是重叠窗口的历史均值。高位信号的 21 项收益、回撤与波动比较，没有一项通过 5% 的 Holm 多重比较校正。融资减速的条件差异来自另一次探索性检验，不是本图的分组结果。本文没有据此构造交易策略，也不把这些结果推广为所有杠杆指标、所有市场的结论。
articleBody_en:
Record margin debt often sounds like a warning that stocks have become overheated. A decline in borrowing can sound like the beginning of the next sell-off. The story is compelling: borrowed money lifts prices, and deleveraging eventually reverses the gains.

For investors, however, a more useful question is: **Does margin debt tell us something that prices have not already told us?**

We examined long-run US margin balances and compared subsequent returns, maximum drawdowns and volatility across financing states. Borrowing cycles are easy to see. Turning those cycles into a dependable entry or exit decision is much harder.

## A cycle is not a countdown

Even after adjusting for inflation, margin balances repeatedly expand, contract and expand again. Using a consistent 10% reversal rule, we identified nine contractions followed by renewed expansion within two reporting segments over 1997–2024.

Their duration varies considerably. Peak-to-trough contractions alone range from two months to thirty months. A financing cycle describes changes in borrowing; it does not schedule the next market decline.

![Figure 1 | Repeated expansions and contractions in margin borrowing. Each reporting segment starts at 100; the panels show within-segment changes, not comparable absolute levels. Sources: FINRA, CPI; Residual Inertia calculations.](assets/insights/margin-debt-cycles-en.svg)

“High” borrowing also needs a reference point. Dollar balances, debt relative to market size, and borrowing growth answer different questions. We use ΔDC to track inflation-adjusted borrowing growth and ΔDS to track growth in borrowing relative to stock prices. We examine them separately rather than treating them as two independent confirmations.

One of the more striking comparisons appears after high ΔDS readings. Average maximum drawdown over the following twelve months is approximately 22.2%, compared with 16.0% across all eligible starts: a gap of 6.2 percentage points.

After removing observation windows that overlap the 2007–2009 financial crisis, however, the averages are 15.7% and 14.1%. The gap falls to 1.5 percentage points.

![Figure 2 | Much of the drawdown gap after high ΔDS readings is concentrated in the financial crisis. Maximum drawdown measures the largest peak-to-subsequent-trough loss within the holding period, not the ending return. Sources: FINRA, CRSP; Residual Inertia calculations.](assets/insights/margin-debt-drawdowns-en.svg)

The crisis plainly matters. But when a signal owes much of its appeal to a few crises, whether the same rule will give useful advance warning next time remains a separate question. Our tests have not established a stable answer.

## How much price information is already in borrowing?

It is unsurprising that prices and borrowing move together. Rising markets change account equity, borrowing capacity and investors' willingness to borrow. Falling markets can reverse those changes. Stock prices also enter the calculation of ΔDS directly.

In our sample, prices more clearly lead borrowing across months before 2010; afterward, contemporaneous co-movement is stronger. Once we account for known price trends, recent returns and prior volatility, financing contraction no longer shows a clear independent increment to subsequent risk.

**The same market move can appear first in prices and then in borrowing statistics. Two indicators do not necessarily provide two pieces of new information.**

There is an interesting exception worth retaining. In the US sample, among similar price states, months in which borrowing was still growing but slowing performed better than months with accelerating borrowing. That conditional difference has not yet become a trading rule validated in an independent sample.

Margin data can still help investors understand how market participants are adjusting their borrowing. But high borrowing does not automatically imply a sell signal, and falling borrowing does not automatically mean risk has cleared. Options and other instruments outside margin accounts can remain active; trading activity itself does not establish an increase in net leverage.

Before adding a financing indicator to a price-based assessment, ask: **Does it provide a new basis for judgment, or repeat a change already visible in prices?** For the margin-financing indicators we have tested, the additional information remains limited.

## Methods and data

This article presents existing research in a public-facing format. It retains the frozen data through year-end 2024 and the original tests, without selecting new parameters for this article. Margin financing means borrowing in customers' securities margin accounts, not all derivatives exposure or corporate balance-sheet debt.

Figure 1 divides monthly margin balances by CPI. The January 1997–January 2010 segment uses historical combined balances; the February 2010 onward segment uses unified FINRA reporting. Each segment is separately rebased. Within each segment, a 10% decline from the running peak confirms contraction; a 10% rise from the subsequent running trough confirms renewed expansion. Peak and trough dates are retrospective; confirmation occurs later.

Let D be nominal margin debt, P the S&P 500 price index, and CPI the consumer price index. ΔDC = 100 × [(D/CPI)t / (D/CPI)t−12 − 1]; ΔDS = 100 × [(D/P)t / (D/P)t−12 − 1]. D/P is not debt divided by aggregate equity market capitalization.

In Figure 2, high ΔDS exceeds the expanding, past-only 80th percentile within the same reporting segment, requiring at least 24 valid prior observations. For signal month t, entry is at the end of t+1 and exit at the end of t+13. CRSP daily SPY total returns, including dividends, produce the wealth path and maximum drawdown. Signal months span January 2000–January 2010 and February 2013–November 2023. The full sample contains 251 starts, including 39 high-signal starts. Removing forward holding windows overlapping October 2007–March 2009 leaves 221 starts, including 25 high-signal starts. The all-start benchmark includes high-signal starts; it is not a normal-financing control group.

The chart shows historical averages over overlapping windows. None of the 21 high-signal comparisons across returns, drawdowns and volatility passes a 5% Holm multiple-comparison adjustment. The conditional slowing result comes from a separate exploratory test, not the groups in this figure. No trading strategy is constructed here, and the findings do not establish conclusions for every leverage indicator or every market.
